data.hypothesis: A serial r-k-c rank-1 update traverses each B row and C row contiguously, potentially improving locality and compiler vectorization across c versus the baseline r-c-k loop. Keeping k in ascending order and zeroing C first preserves the accumulation order and overwrite behavior; this isolates traversal from threading or unrolling.
data.notes: This is the simple serial traversal experiment only; no row-parallelism or unrolling is added. The supplied baseline n=1024 timings average 6.4059 seconds across three samples. No candidate measurements are available yet; correctness, tolerance, and repeated native timings remain for controller evaluation.
transformations: Replace the innermost r-c-k dot-product traversal with a serial r-k-c rank-1 update, streaming contiguous B and C rows.
